messages:
Sam: heads up — ByteCart just filed an escalation: p99 API spikes and intermittent 504s after the 17:42 UTC deploy. Customer says requests that used to be 200–400ms are spiking to 1.8s+. See attached tenant id: bytecart-prod.
Nina: thanks — is this on Hosted or Dedicated? any error logs or OOM traces yet?
Sam: Hosted (prod-gpu pool). I grabbed a few logs — saw repeated allocator failures and GPU OOM-like traces around 17:45. Sample: `ERROR runtime: GPUAlloc failed to reserve 512MB for KV cache (attempt 3)`. Also p95=420ms, p99=1.82s for /v1/generate from 17:30-18:00.
Kevin: sounds like KV growth + fragmentation. Did ByteCart start sending much larger contexts or a new prompt pattern? Any change in avg seq length or concurrent sessions?
Sam: Customer says they pushed a feature that attaches ~6–8k token histories per request for some workflows around 17:40. Concurrent sessions up ~2x.
Nina: that explains it. We saw similar in past incidents where KV entries grew and slab fragmentation pushed alloc attempts up, causing slow alloc fallbacks and request stalls. Can you run the debug kv snapshot for the tenant?
Sam: running now: `rwdctl debug kv-sizes --tenant=bytecart-prod --since=2026-03-16T16:00Z`
rwd-bot: debug job queued (job id=dbg-8921) — results: top_kv_keys: ["session:xyz:ctx": 4.8MB, "session:abc:ctx": 3.6MB, "cache:resp:123": 2.9MB], total_kv=42.1MB, slab_frag_ratio=0.62, alloc_failures=47, evictions=12
Kevin: total_kv 42MB for one tenant on this pool is high. slab_frag_ratio 0.62 means 62% of slab memory is fragmented/unavailable for sizes requested. Alloc_failures indicate we fell back to slow paths. Two immediate mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant KV cap and aggressive eviction, 2) enable allocator defrag heuristics on the pool.
Leo: agreed. Recommend thread mitigation commands:
```
# apply tenant cap + eviction
rwdctl tenant update --id=bytecart-prod --kv-cap=8MB --kv-eviction=aggressive
# tune runtime allocator for defrag window (non-disruptive)
rwdctl runtime tune --pool=prod-gpu --allocator-defrag=on --defrag-passive=60s
# enable backpressure to shed long requests
rwdctl runtime set --pool=prod-gpu --gpu-backpressure=on
```
Kevin: also temporarily route ByteCart to a lower-kv model variant until they trim histories: `route set bytecart-prod -> model:redwood/opt-small:v2-fallback` or enable per-route model fallback for heavy sessions.
Sam: applying tenant cap + eviction now. Will flip back if we see regression.
(rwd-bot): tenant update applied (kv-cap=8MB, eviction=aggressive) — change id tx-7712
Sam: quick update 15m after changes: p95 dropped to 260ms, p99 330ms, 504s gone. Alloc_failures now 3 in last 15m, slab_frag_ratio down to 0.48. Memory usage still elevated but stable.
Nina: great. Next steps: 1) schedule follow-up with ByteCart to advise on trimming session length and adding deduping/summary; 2) long-term platform fixes — enforce per-tenant soft KV quotas, surface per-tenant KV telemetry in Console, and add an automated mitigation playbook (cap+defrag+fallback) for rapid apply; 3) consider allocator size-class compaction improvements and more aggressive periodic defrag for high-churn pools.
Kevin: file a runtime bug with the allocator team (include kv growth repro) — suggest an experiment: enable a background compaction pass that coalesces free tokens across size classes, measure p99 impact.
Sam: opening support ticket and scheduling a remediation call with ByteCart for tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Leo: add postmortem and action items to the incident board. I'll own the follow-up with allocator folks.
Sam: will attach timeline and logs to the ticket (incl. dbg-8921 output). Closing this Slack escalation for now — re-open if any regression. :white_check_mark:
